title: Ofgem publishes the energy price cap for 1 January to 31 March 2027 — a DEADLINE, not a slot, and a confirmation of a number the observation window already fixed a week earlier
source: EST: THE PREFIX IS EXACT HERE AND IS NOT A TAXONOMY ARTIFACT — the primary gives a CEILING, so the specific day is a reasoning estimate sitting on top of a fetched primary. Ofgem's own October-cap release, ofgem.gov.uk/news/changes-energy-price-cap-between-1-october-and-31-december-2026 (published 26 August 2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200), reads under 'Energy price cap level dates': 'The levels for the next periods will be announced by: 25 November 2026 - period 1 January 2027 to 31 March 2027 / 23 February 2027 - period 1 April 2027 to 30 June 2027 / 26 May 2027 - period 1 July 2027 to 30 September 2027'. The word is 'by'. Ofgem states the discretion explicitly on its own sibling pages: 'We may publish before this date if we need to because of external reasons' (ofgem.gov.uk/news/changes-energy-price-cap-between-1-january-and-31-march-2026, published 21 November 2025, fetched direct 2026-09-09). THE DEADLINE HAS BEEN BEATEN ONCE IN THE THREE CYCLES THIS LANE COULD SOURCE: 'by 25 November 2025' resolved on 21 November 2025, four days early (ofgem.gov.uk/press-release/energy-price-cap-will-rise-02-january, publication date 21 November 2025, +0.2% to GBP 1,758 for Jan-Mar 2026, fetched direct); 'by 25 February 2026' resolved ON 25 February 2026 (-7% to GBP 1,641 for Apr-Jun 2026); 'by 26 August 2026' resolved ON 26 August 2026 (+4% for Oct-Dec 2026). Base rate 2 of 3 on the stated day. Also filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix list (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:/OCC:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:/FHFA:) has no slot for a UK sector regulator. Proposed 2026-09-09 by the uk-cpi-2026-10-21 lane; researched and made canonical by its own lane the same day
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-09, superseding proposals/ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2026-11-25.from-uk-cpi-2026-10-21.json (read in full first, per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md). THE PROPOSER'S PLACEMENT SURVIVES; TWO OF ITS CLAIMS DO NOT. WHAT SURVIVES: the Ofgem cap is the single largest known mover of the UK CPI housing-and-household-services line, it steps on 1 Jan / 1 Apr / 1 Jul / 1 Oct, and the January 2027 step is what makes the January CPI print forecastable. WHAT THE RESEARCH CORRECTED. (1) REFUTED - the proposal said 'the January cap is the one quarter where a headline cap number and the bill a household actually pays diverge by the full 5% VAT'. Ofgem quotes the cap VAT-INCLUSIVE; with domestic electricity zero-rated 1 Oct 2026 - 31 Mar 2027 (SI 2026/987), inclusive equals exclusive, so headline EQUALS paid. Ofgem's own words: 'VAT is not included in electricity bills for people covered under the energy price cap between 1 October and 31 December 2026'. There is no divergence, and nothing about it is unique to January - Oct-Dec 2026 is identically zero-rated. (2) IMPRECISE - 'the last cap SET while the zero-rating is in force': the 23 February 2027 announcement is also made while it is in force. The precise statement is that Jan-Mar 2027 is the last cap PERIOD the zero rate covers. THE CONSEQUENCE THE PROPOSAL MISSED, AND IT IS THE POINT: because both Oct-Dec 2026 and Jan-Mar 2027 sit inside the zero rate, THE OCTOBER-TO-JANUARY STEP IS VAT-CLEAN - pure wholesale, network and policy cost. The VAT distortion lands one quarter later, at the Apr-Jun 2027 cap (announced by 23 February 2027, proposed here), which carries the wholesale move PLUS the mechanical 0%-to-5% snap-back on the electricity leg. That is the step to diarise, and it lands in the April 2027 CPI (~2027-05-19, already proposed by the uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01 lane). THE SECOND STRUCTURAL FINDING: 25 NOVEMBER IS NOT WHEN THE NUMBER IS DECIDED. Ofgem's wholesale indexation is 3-1.5-12[3] - a three-month observation window closing roughly 30 working days before the cap period starts. Cornwall Insight dated the equivalent window precisely one cycle ago: 'following the closure of the observation window on 18 November' for the Jan-Mar 2026 cap, announced 21 November 2025. By that construction the Jan-Mar 2027 window closes ~17-18 November 2026 and the cap is arithmetically determined about a WEEK BEFORE Ofgem says it. The announcement is a confirmation, not a print. LIVE FORECAST AT RESEARCH TIME: Cornwall Insight, 26 August 2026, 'bills currently forecast to rise a further 9% in the new year. This would put an average January bill up to GBP 1,872 a year' - driven by 'the conflict in the Middle East', a European summer heatwave, Norwegian supply disruption and Asian demand leaving low winter gas stocks. Their own caveat, quoted: 'The January figure will not be confirmed until November, and there remains a lot of time for wholesale market conditions to shift.' At registration ~9 weeks of the observation window still ran. MPC INTERACTION, STATED HONESTLY: the announcement falls 20 days AFTER the 2026-11-05 MPC and its November Monetary Policy Report, and 22 days BEFORE the 2026-12-17 MPC (boe-decision-2026-12-17, tracked). The Bank forecasts the cap step rather than being surprised by it; what 25 November removes is the December committee's forecast error on that one line, not a policy shock. TIERED LOW: symbols [], and this calendar's whole symbol universe is eight US mega-caps (AAPL AMZN AVGO CRWV GOOG META MRVL MSFT) with no UK listing, no utility, no gilt and no sterling instrument. No house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4/G1) is energy- or sterling-keyed. AN AGGREGATOR CLAIM REJECTED ON THE RECORD: a search-result synthesis asserted the January 2027 cap window ran '19 May to 18 August 2026'. It traces to no primary, contradicts Cornwall Insight's own dated mid-November window statement, and contradicts Ofgem's published 3-1.5-12[3] formula. Not used. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this. Ledger: docs/research/events/ofgem-price-cap-announcement-2026-11-25.md
